newsitem.title: FRANCE: Carat sees six pct 1997 rise in France TV ad spend.
newsitem.headline: Carat sees six pct 1997 rise in France TV ad spend.

text.p: Gross spending on television advertising in France should grow six percent this year, Carat Expert, the research arm of Carat, Europe's largest agency placing advertising space, said on Thursday.
French TV advertising rates are likely to rise by two percent in the period, it added.
Carat Expert was presenting its annual directory of television advertising, Maxi-Book TV 97, at a news conference.

"There should be three to four percent more brands with a television advertising presence, while average advertising budgets should rise two to three percent," said Rene Saal, Carat Expert's managing director.
Spending on television advertising in France rose 7.6 percent to 22.3 billion francs in 1996 after a strong rise of 11.8 percent in 1995 to 20.8 billion francs, Carat Expert said.
Saal estimated that private terrestrial television station TF1 should account for about 50 percent of the market in 1997.
It attracted 51.6 percent of television advertising spending in 1996, but this share fell to 49.2 percent in the first two months of this year, he said.
Carat Expert made no estimates for the market share of other television channels.

"The strongest channels are those which can hold on to their programming schedule for the longest possible time without needing to change it, which would be France 3 and M6, with the weaker ones being TF1 and France 2," Saal said.
France 2 and France 3 are the two public French television channels. M6 is owned by Lyonnaise des Eaux and Luxemburg's CLT, itself part of Audiofina.
Saal added that cable and satellite channels should represent about five percent of the French television advertising market by the year 2000.
By then between 4.5 million and five million homes should be cabled or receiving satellite television, Carat Expert said.
